title: Treatment Mix in Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis: An Allocation Study
intro: Thank you for participating. This survey takes approximately 10 minutes. Your responses are confidential and reported only in aggregate.

computed.label: ADVANCED-THERAPY SHARE
computed.note: Sum of the Q1 percentages for oral systemic agents (r3) and biologic therapy (r4).

questions.text: Which of the following best describes your primary professional role?
How many patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis do you personally manage in a typical month?
questions.instruction: Enter a whole number between 0 and 500.

questions.text: Thinking about all of your moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis patients, what percentage is currently managed primarily with each of the following approaches?
questions.instruction: Enter a whole number in every row. Your answers must sum to exactly 100.

questions.text: You indicated that half or more of your patients receive an oral systemic or biologic therapy. Which factor has been most important in expanding your use of advanced therapies?
What is the single biggest barrier to moving more of your patients to advanced therapies?

options.label: Patient preference for topical or non-drug approaches

questions.text: Which biologic class do you consider first for a biologic-naive patient with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis?
Of your patients on biologic therapy, approximately what percentage achieve clear or almost-clear skin within 6 months?
questions.instruction: Enter a whole number between 0 and 100.

questions.text: What single change would most increase your use of biologic therapy in moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis?
How likely are you to recommend advanced therapy to a colleague treating moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis?
questions.instruction: 0 = Not at all likely, 10 = Extremely likely

seededErrors.description: Docx says the Q1 percentages MUST SUM TO 100; the site accepts any total and never validates the sum.
Docx says IF ADVANCED-THERAPY SHARE < 50 SKIP TO Q3; the site uses < 30, so respondents with shares of 30-49 are wrongly routed into the Q2 deep-dive.
Docx caps the 'Other approaches' row at a maximum of 20; the site accepts up to 100 in that row.
